learningObjective: Reason about the portability constraints of a serialized TensorRT engine across GPU architectures, driver versions and TensorRT major versions.

canonicalClaims.claim: TensorRT plan files are self-contained artifacts that are architecture-specific (compute capability), TensorRT-major-version-specific, and bound to the optimization-profile shape ranges specified at build time.
conditions: Standard build without explicit hardware-compat or version-compat modes.
The runtime is being asked to deserialize on a possibly different device or version.
nonImplications: Does not imply cross-arch/version is impossible; opt-in compatibility modes exist.
Does not imply plans depend on the source ONNX at runtime.

misconceptions.claim: Plans depend on the source ONNX at deserialization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Plans are self-contained binaries; the ONNX is not needed at runtime.

misconceptions.claim: Plans are portable across all NVIDIA GPUs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Plans are compiled for a specific compute capability by default.
TRT does not guarantee cross-major-version compatibility for plans.

misconceptions.claim: Input shape ranges are inferred at run time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ranges must be specified as optimization profiles at build time.
